proposals.citation: dedr[entry 156];varghese2015palakkad[Appendix B3, item 105, Alu Kurumba, Banigudisola]
proposals.evidence: DEDR156(a) gives Tamil appaṉ, Malayalam appan, Kannada appa and Kodagu appë father. The selected survey appa/appan/appe responses retain the same locally elicited father sense; minority-lect extensions are comparative. This nursery/honorific family does not by itself distinguish shared inheritance from regional diffusion, and other languages’ mother/aunt senses are not substituted. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.citation: dedr[entry 2248];varghese2015palakkad[Appendix B3, item 87, Alu Kurumba, Banigudisola]
proposals.evidence: DEDR2248 gives Tamil/Malayalam kōḻi fowl, Kota kōy, Kodagu kōḷi, Kannada kōḻi and Tulu kōri/kōḷi. These southern survey kōyi/koyɨ/kōḷi/kośi/kojī-type responses are comparative lect extensions, retaining the glide, lateral and palatal/sibilant variants. The source chicken sense is compatible with fowl; this does not merge them with the distinct central-Dravidian kor family. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.citation: dedr[entry 3296];blairetal2012kurumba[Appendix C, printed p. 258, item 72, list ANSK, Kotagiri Alu Kurumba]
proposals.evidence: DEDR3296 gives Kannada tuṭi/toḍi, Tulu duḍi and Kota tuc lip. The survey dental/retroflex and voicing variants are preserved; Badaga/Sholaga and Alu Kurumba are comparative lect extensions, and Kota tus is compared with the specifically attested Kota tuc. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.citation: dedr[entry 561];blairetal2012kurumba[Appendix C, printed p. 259, item 89, list ANSK, Kotagiri Alu Kurumba]
proposals.evidence: DEDR561 gives Kannada ugur, Tulu uguru, Kodagu oy and Kurukh orᵒx finger-nail. Survey uguru/ugarɨ and glide variants are comparative regional matches, with initial v-/a- and medial-y notation preserved. Kurukh orox matches the corrected rhotic spelling; the primary explicitly rejects Grignard’s oṛᵒx, so survey retroflex-r forms are held separately. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.citation: dedr[entry 4635];varghese2015palakkad[Appendix B3, item 76, Alu Kurumba, Banigudisola]
proposals.evidence: DEDR4635 gives Tamil mañcaḷ, Malayalam maññaḷ/mañña, Kannada mañjaḷa, Kodagu mañja and Tulu mañjaḷu turmeric or turmeric-yellow. The selected simple southern survey mañja/mañjal-type turmeric responses are comparative lect extensions preserving palatal nasal/stop spelling, final-lateral loss and vowel notation; no longer compound is reduced to this stem. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
